task: Integrate two 10-frame character sprite sheets in a React app using CSS Modules: a wave animation and a sink-below-the-screen animation.

sink.note: This asset has been normalized from the generated 2x5 sheet into the same 10-frame horizontal 400x450 format as the wave sheet.

intendedBehavior.idle: Show frame 1 of the wave sheet as the normal resting character.
intendedBehavior.wave: Play the 10-frame wave once when the character first appears, or when the app explicitly triggers the wave.
intendedBehavior.hover: When the user hovers the character, switch to the sink sheet and play frames 1 through 10 so the character appears to sink below the bottom edge of the viewport/container.
intendedBehavior.mouseLeave: Return to the normal idle pose. Do not crossfade between sprite sheets.
intendedBehavior.important: The bottom of the sprite must be clipped by a wrapper with overflow: hidden so the sinking motion reads as going below the screen/container edge.

React: Use one wrapper element that controls clipping and one sprite element inside it.
Track animation state with a small React state value such as 'idle', 'wave', or 'sink' only if CSS hover alone is not enough.
For the hover sink interaction, CSS-only is acceptable: use the sink sprite as the hover animation while the idle state uses the first wave frame.

cssRequirements: The visible sprite frame is 400px wide by 450px tall before any visual scaling.
Both animations move background-position-x from 0px to -3600px.
Use steps(9, end) because there are 10 frames and 9 transitions from the first frame to the last frame.
Do not use opacity fades, crossfades, motion blur, or smooth interpolation between sprite frames.
Use overflow: hidden on the clipping wrapper.
Anchor the character to bottom center so the sink animation visually disappears below the edge.
If the character is displayed smaller, scale the sprite consistently rather than changing frame math independently.
interactionNotes: Do not run wave and sink animations at the same time.
If the wave is automatic on page load, let it finish before hover can start the sink animation, or allow hover to interrupt it cleanly.
The sink animation should use forwards while hovered so the character stays almost fully hidden after sinking.
When hover ends, remove the sink animation and immediately restore the idle first frame.
If a smoother reappearance is desired later, create a separate rise animation by playing the sink frames in reverse.
acceptanceCriteria: The same character occupies the same 400x450 frame size in both assets.
The idle pose does not jump when switching from the wave sheet to the sink sheet.
Hover makes the character appear to descend below the bottom edge rather than simply fade out.
The wrapper clips anything below its bottom boundary.
The sink finishes with only a small amount of hair visible or the character almost fully hidden.
Leaving hover restores the idle character cleanly.
No phantom limbs, crossfading, or blended frames are introduced by CSS.
